01-brief: Floor Plan Studio turns a structured small-office brief into a dimensioned layout. This walkthrough uses the built-in synthetic office. Room minimums and maximums are hard requirements. Targets and zoning are preferences.
02-baseline: Here is the baseline layout. The constraint solver placed rooms around a fixed corridor and service reserve. Select a room to see its measured dimensions, capacity, and indicative furniture.
03-validation: The independent report checks the exported geometry. It records measurements, requirements, and the limits of what was verified. It also shows which reviews still need professional judgment.
04-stale: Now the meeting room needs at least twenty-four square metres. Editing the brief makes the old result stale. Both downloads are disabled until the current revision passes validation.
05-revised: Regeneration returns a new candidate. The revised meeting room meets the new minimum. The SVG and JSON exports now belong to the checked revision.
06-conflict: The area-conflict example asks for more room area than fits inside the shell. The application explains the contradiction and keeps export disabled. This is a feasibility study for the encoded geometry. Real building approval needs qualified review.
